content.comment_body: Hello, which transducer should I use to connect an ORP probe to an analog port of [product_name] [version_no]? Thank you in advance.
What is an ORP probe? The onboard analog input of a base module of [product_name] [version_no] only works with 0-10V voltage signals.
An ORP probe is designed to measure chlorine. Just like a PT100 sensor needs a converter to produce a 0-10V signal, this probe requires a transducer because it cannot be connected directly.
Please mention the manufacturer and the model of your ORP probe.
I'm unable to locate this probe online. Do you have a link or a datasheet?

Hello [user_name], I think what [user_name] is seeking is the output range for your ORP probe. Recalling a previous project, our ORP probe produced a ±100mV output voltage. To convert such a signal to 0-10V for the analog input of [product_name], you could use a signal conditioner like the one found at [url]. Knowing the output range of your ORP probe will help us give more accurate advice. There are various manufacturers of signal conditioners, such as Phoenix Contacts, Omega, and Automation Direct. Please research based on your specific needs. Keep in mind, however, that the ORP probe output is quite non-linear, so take care when interpreting the conditioned voltage values. Hope this helps, [user_name]

We need the output specification of your sensor. With that information, it's easier to determine a suitable solution. You can find modules online that convert small voltage ranges to 0-10V. For instance, try searching for: Positive and negative voltage small signal conversion module - 0-20mV/5V/10V/20mA bipolar signal conditioning.
Thanks everyone for your help. My measurement is limited to microamperes, so I’ll need to amplify the signal first.
